objective: Integrate seams S1 (producer→consumer) and S2 (producer→engine) against frozen C1/C2: create tests/integration/test_timeout_seam.py (new, 3 tests: real-module round-trip, missing-timeout default + draft-key fallback, engine boundary) and docs/wire-contract-consistency.md (new, read-only diff of producer.py/engine.py/consumer.py against the C1/C2 specs), patch any seam defect found only inside T01/T02 owned paths (integration-only fix ownership), and record every patch in the checkpoint as a deviation.

concepts: seam round-trip through real modules (no mocks)
integration-only fix ownership (patch rights limited to T01/T02 owned paths)
failure-scenario gating: every seam needs a bad-input case, not just the happy path

inputs: T01 output: modified pipeline/consumer.py (S1 conformance to C1)
T02 output: tests/test_wire_contract.py (C1/C2 regression suite to run and cross-check)
seam definitions S1/S2 and E2E scenarios E1-E3 (integration-plan.json)

allowed_dependencies.what: modified pipeline/consumer.py — S1 conformance to C1 (read + run, patch-allowed as integration-only fix)
tests/test_wire_contract.py — C1/C2 regression suite to run and cross-check (read + run, patch-allowed as integration-only fix)

non_goals: Do not restructure pipeline/ modules or move functions between them
Do not patch files outside T01/T02 owned paths (pipeline/consumer.py, tests/test_wire_contract.py)
Do not modify tests/test_producer.py, tests/test_consumer.py, or tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py
Do not change E2E gate commands or acceptance ids from stage-contract.json
implementation_constraints: Seam tests use only real modules (no mocks): producer.make_job → consumer.job_timeout and → engine.run_job
Patch rights: pipeline/consumer.py and tests/test_wire_contract.py only, minimal diff; each patch is recorded as a deviation in checkpoints/T03.json with file, diff summary, and reason
The consistency doc must state, per C1 field: producer value, engine read, consumer resolution, and a verdict (consistent / drifted)
Stdlib unittest only; module runs via python -m unittest tests.integration.test_timeout_seam from the repo root

deliverables.what: package marker so unittest can import the module
read-only consistency diff of producer/engine/consumer against C1/C2 with per-field verdicts

acceptance_tests.description: Round-trip: job = make_job('s1', {'cmd': 'x'}, timeout_ms=500); job_timeout(job) returns 500 and run_job(job, 400) returns status 'done'
Bad input: job = {'id': 's2', 'payload': {}} (no timeout keys) → job_timeout returns 30000 without raising; run_job(job, 31000) returns status 'timeout' via the default path
Draft-key fallback and engine boundary: job_timeout({'timeout': 123}) returns 123; run_job(make_job('s3', {}, timeout_ms=100), 100) returns status 'done' (work_ms == timeout_ms is not >)
docs/wire-contract-consistency.md exists and records a 'consistent' verdict per C1 field (timeout_ms emission, engine read, consumer resolution, default 30000)
acceptance_tests.evidence: File exists at docs/wire-contract-consistency.md; grep for 'timeout_ms' and 'consistent' in docs/wire-contract-consistency.md

failure_cases.scenario: T01's consumer.py carries a seam defect the fixture e2e test cannot catch (e.g. fallback and timeout_ms branches swapped)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: T03 patches pipeline/consumer.py (owned by T01, patch-allowed), records the deviation in checkpoints/T03.json, and re-runs T03-AT1 through T03-AT4 until green

failure_cases.scenario: A defect belongs to a file outside T01/T02 owned paths (e.g. producer.py or engine.py)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: T03 stops the branch and emits a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST or CORE_SEAM_BLOCKER in its checkpoint instead of patching the file

handoff.notes: Checkpoint must list: patches applied (file, diff summary, reason), per-field consistency verdicts, and the red→green state of T02's consumer-resolution test if T01's fix landed within T03's window. A green T03 gate is the precondition for T04's final evidence.
